result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 2 (this pass): fixed both TEST-RUNNER-flagged causes, plus one additional blocking bug discovered while confirming the fix (documented below, not silently expanded scope). (a) priv/repo/migrations/20260819045553_add_sub_process_parent_columns.exs was never registered in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest -- added {20_260_819_045_553, Letflow.Repo.Migrations.AddSubProcessParentColumns, "20260819045553_add_sub_process_parent_columns.exs"} in version-sorted position (between 20260819000003 and 20260820000001), matching every other entry's exact {version, module, filename} tuple shape. (b) lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's @node_type_map had no "SUB_PROCESS" => :SUB_PROCESS entry -- added it as the map's last entry, matching the existing "TIMER" => :TIMER / "HUMAN_TASK" => :HUMAN_TASK entries' exact shape.

After applying both, ran the scoped subset per the handoff instructions and found the two assigned failure classes gone (confirmed: zero occurrences of Postgrex 42703 or node_type_not_yet_implemented/unknown_node_type anywhere in the scoped run's output), but 9 of 10 EngineSubProcessTest tests still failed with a NEW, third failure mode: `** (RuntimeError) operation :rollback is rolling back unexpectedly` raised from inside Letflow.Engine.persist/9's own Repo.transaction() call. Root-caused by instrumenting each Multi step (temporary IO.inspect/rescue, removed before finishing -- lib/letflow/engine.ex and lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex are otherwise unchanged besides the fix below): Letflow.Engine.SubProcess.append_instance_started_event_for_child/8 and append_sub_process_completed_event/8 both reused the caller's own `idempotency_key` (create/2's or complete_task/3's own request-level key) VERBATIM for the child's own INSTANCE_STARTED event and for the parent-stream SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED event. `event_idempotency.idempotency_key` (20260816120006_create_event_idempotency.exs) is uniquely indexed schema-wide, not per-instance, so reusing the same key for two DIFFERENT events appended in the SAME transaction (parent's own INSTANCE_STARTED + child's own INSTANCE_STARTED, both keyed off the same request idempotency_key) collides: EventStore.append/2 (which opens its OWN nested Repo.transaction/1 internally) hits its claim_idempotency Multi step returning {:error, {:duplicate_idempotency_key, original_event}}, and because that Repo.transaction/1 is nested inside persist/9's own already-open outer transaction, Ecto's internal rollback signal for the inner failure is not bubbled cleanly to the outer Multi -- Ecto raises the generic RuntimeError instead of a typed error tuple (this is Ecto's own documented nested-transaction limitation, not a new architecture decision on my part). This is a genuine implementation defect introduced in this same run's iteration 1 (SubProcess module), directly blocking verification of virtually every REQ-062 acceptance criterion including the two fixes just made -- fixed within this run per core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything rule rather than filed forward, matching the same rationale iteration 1's own reconstruction.ex fix used. Fix: derive a distinct, collision-free idempotency_key at both call sites -- `"#{parent_idempotency_key}::sub_process_start::#{child_instance_id}"` for the child's own INSTANCE_STARTED event, `"#{idempotency_key}::sub_process_completed::#{parent_instance_id}::#{child_instance_id}"` for the parent-stream SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED event -- both still traceable back to the originating request's own key, both guaranteed unique since child_instance_id is a freshly minted UUID. No signature changes -- both fixes are internal to the two private functions that build event_attrs.

Verification commands actually run: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> 'Compiling ... Generated letflow app' (exit 0). `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix ecto.migrate` -> 'Migrations already up' (clean, no pending migration). `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs` -> '42 tests, 6 failures' (down from the 9 failures present after fixing only (a)+(b), and from the original 86-failure full-suite run TEST-RUNNER reported) -- all remaining 6 failures are in EngineSubProcessTest only (engine_test.exs is fully green), and are two FURTHER distinct, deeper bugs, out of this rework iteration's assigned scope: (i) a CaseClauseError in Letflow.Engine.append_sub_process_completion_cascade_multi/6 (engine.ex:1678) against a %TokenRecord{} it doesn't pattern-match, hit by AC3/AC8's SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_OUTPUT and SUB_PROCESS_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION tests plus AC4 and AC5's own child-completion tests (4 of the 6); (ii) a Protocol.UndefinedError -- Jason.Encoder not implemented for Letflow.EventStore.Registry.ValidationFailure -- hit by AC3/AC8's SUB_PROCESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION test (1 of the 6); the SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_INPUT test (the 6th) fails for a related but distinct reason visible in the same output. None of these three overlap with the migration-registration or node_type_map causes this rework iteration was scoped to fix, and none overlap with the idempotency_key collision fixed above (confirmed by their distinct exception types and stack traces, captured in full in this run's own test output). Did not touch test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs per the rework instruction. mix format --check-formatted run on every touched file: lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex and lib/letflow/engine.ex (touched only by since-removed debug instrumentation, net zero diff) both clean; lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex reformatted once (`mix format`) then verified clean; lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's own format complaint (a pre-existing, unrelated multi-line boolean expression around line 930) was confirmed via `git stash` to already exist before this pass's own single-line node_type_map addition -- left untouched, out of scope.
